stories.headline: Canada sets aside 45,000 extra PR places for spouses of Canadians in 2027
stories.summary: IRCC says it will use extra permanent residence spaces in 2027 to clear applications that are already waiting, including up to 45,000 for spouses, common-law partners and dependent children of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who live in Canada. A further 100,000 places will go to workers already in Canadian communities, chosen with the provinces. No new programme is opening, and people who have already applied do not need to contact IRCC.
stories.tip: If your spousal PR file is pending, keep your address, passport and contact details up to date in your IRCC account so nothing slows it down.

stories.headline: Canada makes its rural immigration route to PR permanent
stories.summary: Canada has turned its Rural Community Immigration Pilot into a permanent programme, with 5,500 admission spaces planned in the 2027-2029 levels plan. The 14 current communities, including Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Brandon and Moose Jaw, stay in, and more will be added later. Candidates still need a job offer from an employer the community has designated, plus a community recommendation.
stories.tip: Only trust job offers you can match to the community's official list of designated employers, and never pay anyone for a 'rural job offer'.

stories.headline: UK student visa applications down 20% in a year, care worker applications down 61%
stories.summary: Home Office figures released on 12 November show 349,900 student main applications in the year to October 2026, 20% fewer than a year earlier, while student dependant applications fell 32%. Skilled Worker applications dropped 42% and Health and Care Worker applications fell 61%. The cuts follow tighter rules on dependants, salaries and overseas care recruitment.
stories.tip: Fewer applicants does not mean easier approval: prepare full funds proof and a clear study plan, and check your university is still sponsoring Nigerian students.

stories.headline: New Zealand won't grant parents residence while a child is unlawful
stories.summary: Immigration New Zealand says that for residence applications lodged from 12 November 2026, a parent or other secondary applicant cannot be approved while a dependent child is in the country without a valid visa. The child must first get a proper visa or leave New Zealand, and dropping the child from the application does not get around the rule. Applications lodged before 12 November are decided under the old rules.
stories.tip: If any child in your family has an expired New Zealand visa, sort out their status before you lodge a residence application.

stories.headline: Nearly half of Nigerian Schengen visa applications refused in 2025
stories.summary: A Foreign Affairs ministry analysis reported by Sunday Punch and BusinessDay puts Nigeria's Schengen refusal rate at 46.9% in 2025, with Belgium, Spain and France refusing the most. Failed Schengen applications alone cost Nigerians about €11.5 million in fees that are never refunded. The same report puts UK refusals at 35.4% in early 2026 and Canadian study permit refusals at about 75%.
stories.tip: Before paying any visa fee, check that your bank statements, ties to Nigeria and travel plan clearly match the visa you are asking for.

stories.headline: Germany's Lagos consulate to add visa counters before year end
stories.summary: Germany's Consul General in Lagos, Daniel Krull, said on 6 November that the consulate will open more visa counters before the end of 2026 and work with outside service providers to release more appointments. More files will also be sent to a German processing centre in Europe to cut delays. A document checking centre for Nigerians applying to German universities is planned in Lagos, but no date was given.
stories.tip: Book German visa appointments only through the official consulate and service provider websites, and check often for newly released slots.

stories.headline: Australia may make students park funds in an Australian bank first
stories.summary: Australia's Home Affairs department is consulting on tougher Genuine Student rules and new proof-of-funds options. Three of the four options would make applicants hold money in an Australian bank account in their own name before applying, from half of total course and living costs up to a full first year. No decision has been made; submissions close on 23 November 2026.
stories.tip: If you plan to study in Australia in 2027, start building documented savings now and watch homeaffairs.gov.au for the final money rules.

stories.headline: Canada keeps 2027 targets: 380,000 new PRs, 150,000 new students
stories.summary: Canada's new immigration plan, released with the federal budget on 5 November, holds permanent resident admissions at 380,000 a year for 2027 to 2029. New temporary arrivals are capped at 370,000 a year, split into 220,000 workers and 150,000 students. Ottawa also plans to give permanent status to many people already in Canada on temporary permits.
stories.tip: Study permit places stay tight, so apply early with a strong study plan and clear proof of funds.

stories.headline: US ends open-ended student stay: F-1 degree students get 4 years
stories.summary: A US Homeland Security rule that took effect on 15 September 2026 replaces the old 'duration of status' with a fixed end date on the I-94 record. Degree students get up to four years and language students up to 24 months. Staying longer means applying to USCIS for an extension, and a refusal can leave a student with no grace period.
stories.tip: Check the admit-until date on your I-94 after every entry, and plan long courses, like PhDs, with an extension in mind.

stories.headline: UK sets 10 years as the normal wait for permanent settlement
stories.summary: The Home Secretary told Parliament on 2 November that most migrants will now wait ten years before settling, up from five. Higher earners above £50,271 and some public service workers can still settle after five years, and the top earners after three. Applicants must also show clean records, strong English, no public debts and steady National Insurance payments. No start date was given in the announcement.
stories.tip: If you plan to settle in the UK, keep your pay slips, tax records and English results organised from day one, and watch gov.uk for the start date.

stories.headline: US now requires a health declaration from every air passenger
stories.summary: From 3 November, everyone flying to the United States, whatever their nationality, must sign a CDC form saying they have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the previous 21 days. Airlines must check the form before boarding, and it also applies to people connecting through a US airport. The order is set to run until 18 December unless CDC changes it.
stories.tip: Fill in the form at check-in or at the airport, and carry your travel history details in case the airline asks.

stories.headline: New Zealand opens six-month graduate work visa on 16 November
stories.summary: Immigration New Zealand will start accepting a new Short-Term Graduate Work Visa on 16 November 2026. It gives six months of open work rights to graduates of full-time courses at levels 5 to 7 that last at least 24 weeks and do not already qualify for a Post-Study Work Visa. Applicants need NZ$5,000 in funds and must apply within three months of their student visa ending; students whose visa expired before 16 August are out.
stories.tip: Check your student visa expiry date and course level now, and gather your medical certificate, chest X-ray and bank statement before applications open.

stories.headline: UK Budget plans to keep two-year Graduate visa for some universities' students
stories.summary: The 28 October Budget says graduates of universities with strong immigration compliance and good job outcomes will keep a two-year Graduate visa, softening the planned cut to 18 months from 1 January 2027. The government has not yet said which universities qualify, what counts as good outcomes, or when this starts. Until rules are published, the 18-month cut stays the working assumption for applications made from 1 January.
stories.tip: If you finish your course soon, apply for the Graduate visa before 31 December 2026 to lock in two years, and ask your university about its compliance status before you pay a deposit.

stories.headline: Nigeria extends UK passport clinics to 27 November
stories.summary: The Nigeria Immigration Service has pushed its special passport exercise in the UK from 30 October to 27 November 2026. London and Manchester run from 3 to 27 November, while Aberdeen and Cardiff only open from 3 to 6 November. Only people who already booked online are served, and cash is not accepted at the venues.
stories.tip: Book your slot on the High Commission portal now and bring your application form, payment slip, appointment printout, return envelope and old passport.

stories.headline: More Nigerian UK study applications withdrawn as universities fear refusals
stories.summary: A report citing a Financial Times analysis of Home Office data says 22.7% of Nigerian student visa applications were withdrawn in the first half of 2026, up from 4.5% a year earlier. The report links the jump to universities pulling offers early, because they must now keep visa refusals under 5% or risk losing their licence. The figures are secondhand, so treat them as a trend, not an official count.
stories.tip: Hold your CAS and visa application until you have clear funds proof and strong study ties, and confirm your offer is still live before paying deposits.

stories.headline: New Zealand refuses 34% of student visas, names Nigeria in fraud warning
stories.summary: Between July and September 2026, Immigration New Zealand turned down about a third of full-fee student visa applications, against 13% the year before. The agency says it found altered and reused documents, and named Nigeria among five countries where it saw fraud concerns, with master's courses checked hardest. It stressed this is about individual applications, not every Nigerian applicant.
stories.tip: Use only your own genuine documents, never reuse bank statements an agent gives you, and make sure your funds proof matches your real finances.

stories.headline: Canada visitor visa wait for Nigerians climbs to 103 days
stories.summary: IRCC's latest processing estimates put visitor visas from Nigeria at about 103 days, up from roughly 84 to 87 days a month earlier. Study permits from Nigeria also slipped, from 9 weeks to 10, while work permits held at 10 weeks. IRCC says these are estimates, not promises.
stories.tip: Apply at least four months before you must travel, and do not buy a ticket until your visa is approved.
stories.alt: A hand holding a Canadian passport

stories.headline: German missions warn Nigerians: we don't work with visa agents
stories.summary: The German embassy in Abuja and consulate in Lagos said on X that they use no visa agents and that nobody can promise approval, a job or a faster slot. Booking an appointment through the official system costs nothing. The warning followed reports of applicants who paid large sums for fake offers.
stories.tip: Use only the official German mission and VFS pages, and never pay anyone who guarantees a visa or an appointment.

stories.headline: Japan raises residence permit fees, permanent residence now ¥200,000
stories.summary: From 1 October 2026, Japan charges more for extending a stay, changing status and permanent residence. Extensions and status changes now cost between ¥10,000 and ¥75,000 depending on how long the stay granted is, while permanent residence jumps from ¥10,000 to ¥200,000. Certificates of Eligibility for new arrivals stay free.
stories.tip: Budget for the new fee tier before you renew, and confirm the exact amount on the Immigration Services Agency website.

stories.headline: UK and Nigeria vow tougher action on visa fraud and fake documents
stories.summary: After talks in London on 6 October, UK and Nigerian officials agreed to work together on visa fraud, organised immigration crime and better document checks. They also pledged to support safe returns of people who abuse the system. No change to UK visa rules for ordinary Nigerian travellers was announced.
stories.tip: Submit only genuine, verifiable documents and use the official gov.uk site, because forged papers can lead to refusal and long bans.
stories.credit: Stock image: Christopher Elison / Flickr, CC BY 2.0

stories.headline: UK student money goes up on 30 November
stories.summary: Students must show £1,570 a month for London and £1,203 outside London from 30 November 2026, up from £1,529 and £1,171. For a 9-month course that is £14,130 or £10,827.
stories.tip: If your documents are ready, apply before 30 November to use the lower figure.

stories.headline: US visas for Nigerians now processed only in Lagos
stories.summary: Routine US visa services at the Abuja embassy ended on 1 August 2026. Appointments, fees and interviews all go through the Lagos consulate. The partial visa suspension, visa bonds and immigrant visa pauses remain in force.
stories.tip: Book through the official US visa site only. Anyone selling 'Abuja slots' is a scammer.

stories.headline: Most US visitor and student visas suspended for Nigerians
stories.summary: Since 1 January 2026, new B-1/B-2 visitor visas and F, M and J student and exchange visas are suspended for Nigerians without a valid US visa. Visas issued before then were not cancelled.
stories.tip: If you already hold a valid US visa, keep it valid and don't overstay it.

stories.headline: Australia stops most onshore switches to student visas
stories.summary: From 2 October 2026, most temporary visa holders can't apply for a student visa inside Australia, and family members can't be added to a new student visa except in limited cases. The graduate visa fee rose to A$5,750 in July.
stories.tip: Plan to apply from Nigeria, and decide early whether your family is coming with you.

stories.headline: Expired BRP cards stop working at the end of 2026
stories.summary: The Home Office lets expired BRPs be used for some purposes only until 31 December 2026. You can't travel on an expired BRP. Your eVisa is now the proof of your status.
stories.tip: Log into your UKVI account and check your passport is linked before you travel.

stories.headline: UK graduate visa shrinks to 18 months on 1 January
stories.summary: Bachelor's and master's graduates who apply on or after 1 January 2027 get 18 months instead of 2 years. It is the application date that counts. PhD graduates keep 3 years.
stories.tip: Finished your degree this year? Submit your Graduate visa application before 31 December.

stories.headline: Canada raises student funds as money proof tops refusals
stories.summary: Study permit applicants outside Quebec must now show CAD 23,448 for living costs, plus tuition and travel. A study of June 2026 decisions found 47% of refusals came down to weak financial documents.
stories.tip: Show steady savings with a clear source. A big deposit last month looks borrowed.

stories.headline: Nigeria has West Africa's highest Schengen refusal rate
stories.summary: Nearly 46% of Nigerian Schengen applications were refused in the latest EU figures, against an 18% global average. The €90 fee is not refunded, and appeals must be filed within 15 days.
stories.tip: Show strong ties to Nigeria, a clear day-by-day plan and bank activity that looks normal.

stories.headline: Care worker visa from abroad is closed, but agents still sell it
stories.summary: The UK stopped sponsoring care workers and senior care workers from overseas on 22 July 2025. Any 'care job with sponsorship' offered to someone in Nigeria for a fee is fake.
stories.tip: Never pay for a job offer or a Certificate of Sponsorship.

stories.headline: France raises university fees for non-EU students
stories.summary: From the 2026/27 year, French public universities charge most non-EU students €2,895 a year for a bachelor's and €3,941 for a master's. Students already enrolled are not affected.
stories.tip: Search for scholarships early, because only a small share of students get fee waivers.

stories.headline: Korea bars 20 universities from sponsoring student visas
stories.summary: Korea's education ministry stopped 20 universities and language programmes from issuing student visas for one year from fall 2026. Students admitted there cannot get a D-2 visa through them.
stories.tip: Before paying a deposit, ask the school in writing if it can sponsor visas this year.

stories.headline: New Zealand widens post-study work visa from 16 November
stories.summary: From 16 November 2026, people with a bachelor's degree plus a full-time New Zealand graduate diploma can qualify for a post-study work visa in their field. Students can already work 25 hours a week during term.
stories.tip: Pick a course that leads to work in a high-demand field if you want to stay after study.

stories.headline: UK student visa delays leave applicants missing course start dates
stories.summary: Universities report students stuck waiting for visas well beyond the three-week standard, with some cases taking up to four months and even the £500 priority service affected. Study visa applications fell 19% to 352,500 in the year to September 2026. The Home Office says straightforward applications are still being decided on time.
stories.tip: Choose the priority service only if you can afford it, and book your appointment as early as your CAS allows.
stories.credit: Stock image: barbourians / Flickr, CC BY-SA 2.0

stories.headline: Canada Express Entry rewards high-wage jobs from 3 November
stories.summary: From 3 November 2026, Express Entry gives new points for a qualifying job offer or at least a year of Canadian work in a high-wage occupation, worth up to 100 points for an offer. A job offer will no longer need an LMIA to count, though IRCC will check it is genuine. Scores in the pool will be recalculated and draws will pause for up to two weeks while that happens.
stories.tip: If you have a genuine high-wage Canadian job offer, update your Express Entry profile before 3 November.
stories.credit: Stock image: striatic / Flickr, CC BY 2.0
